clarification_questions.question: What is the physical state of the material at the probe tip - a soft solid tissue surface that can be brought into tight contact with a probe head, or a surface that cannot be contacted?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: ATR requires tight contact with liquids, pastes or soft solids, so this decides whether an ATR-based route can be used at all.

clarification_questions.question: Is the tissue opaque and strongly scattering at the probe, or can light pass through a defined layer of it?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The optical regime decides between contact and reflection geometries and transmission geometries for any shortlisted method.

clarification_questions.question: Are the first measurements planned on excised tissue samples or on tissue in the operating field?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The supplied tissue work is on excised samples, so the answer decides whether this is a bench feasibility study or a clinical use question.

clarification_questions.question: What independent reference standard (for example histopathology) will label each sample, and what sensitivity and specificity must be reached to go ahead?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: Without a reference label and agreed numbers no discrimination model can be validated or judged.

clarification_questions.question: What fiber link length, sterility, disinfection and biocompatibility constraints apply at the operating field?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: These constraints can rule out a probe or a fiber type before any measurement is attempted.

clarification_questions.question: Has the tissue's fluorescence background at the intended Raman excitation wavelength been measured?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: Strong fluorescence can swamp Raman bands and would remove Raman from the shortlist.

solution_options.fusion_note: Both methods must look at the same small tissue area and their data must be aligned to a common time step, because alternating separate probes cannot guarantee the same spot and the acquisition rates differ. assessment.chemometrics_note: Tissue classification needs calibration or classification models (for example PCA or PLS-DA) built on labelled samples and validated on held-out samples or patients; a model is specific to the tissue matrix and tumour type and must be rebuilt when either changes.
assessment.realtime_tracking_note: Real-time use needs fast acquisition and a fiber link that keeps the spectrometer away from the measurement point; if two methods are combined, their different acquisition rates must be aligned to a common time step.
assessment.future_direction: If the bench work identifies the most informative spectral regions, a compact multisensor or LED-based sensor could be a later development step, following the described sequence of lab trials, then a chemometric model or a customised system.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If the tissue fluoresces strongly at the Raman excitation, or if the MIR fiber link from the measurement point cannot be realised, the balance shifts toward Raman or toward the combined MIR-ATR + Raman option; the team's go/no-go numbers would also change the choice.
proposal.next_step: Run the bench feasibility test on representative tumour and healthy tissue samples against histology before any patient use is considered.

assessment.brief_answer: Nothing supplied covers regulatory approval or clinical readiness, so starting on patients next month is not supported by this material. Technically, the sources give the strongest tissue-classification precedent for MIR-ATR, with Raman (the team's proposal) also worth testing and a combined MIR-ATR + Raman option as a later hypothesis. Next step: a bench feasibility test on representative tumour and healthy tissue against histology, with go/no-go numbers agreed with the team.

assessment.chemometrics_note: Tissue classification needs calibration or classification models (for example PCA or PLS-DA) built on labelled samples and validated on held-out samples or patients; a model is specific to the tissue matrix and tumour type and must be rebuilt when either changes.
assessment.realtime_tracking_note: Real-time use needs fast acquisition and a fiber link that keeps the spectrometer away from the measurement point; if two methods are combined, their different acquisition rates must be aligned to a common time step.

Next step: a bench feasibility test on representative tumour and healthy tissue against histology, with go/no-go numbers agreed with the team.
